keyframes.prompt: Vertical 2:3 underwater macro nature photo in a clear freshwater pond, side view. The flat water surface runs straight across the top of the frame at 85 percent of the frame height from the bottom, seen from just below. Soft green-tinted clear water with gentle light rays from the surface. A few thin green underwater plant stems with fine feathery leaves rise from the brown muddy pond bottom through the horizontal center of the frame, with softly blurred green plants far behind. Among the plant stems, in the center of the frame, a small dome-shaped silvery air bubble is held in a thin white silk sheet attached to the stems, about one fifth of the frame width, with its open side facing down. Just below the water surface, directly above the air bubble, an adult diving bell spider hangs head down on a plant stem: a dark brown body with long dark legs, about one sixth of the frame width including the legs, and a shiny silver air bubble covering its abdomen. Keep everything important away from the left and right edges. Only one spider. No text, no watermark.

Edit this image. Keep the water surface, the plant stems, the pond bottom, the background, lighting and camera angle exactly the same. The spider has moved down into the air bubble. The silvery dome-shaped air bubble stays in the same place among the stems, but it is now bigger, about one third of the frame width. The spider sits inside the bubble in its center, upside down, head facing down toward the open bottom of the bubble, clearly visible through the bubble. The spider keeps the same size. No spider near the water surface. Only one spider. No text, no watermark.

Edit this image. Keep the water surface, the plant stems, the pond bottom, the air bubble, the background, lighting and camera angle exactly the same. The spider stays inside the bubble in the same place, just below the egg sac, guarding it. Only one spider. No text, no watermark.

The egg sac has opened: it is now torn and empty, in the same place. Dozens of tiny pale yellowish-brown baby spiders, each about one fortieth of the frame width, crawl on the silk inside the air bubble around the torn egg sac. The mother spider stays inside the bubble in the same place. No text, no watermark.

Edit this image. Keep the water surface, the plant stems, the pond bottom, the air bubble, the torn egg sac, the background, lighting and camera angle exactly the same. The mother spider and the other baby spiders are gone. One young spider stays inside the air bubble, in the center of the bubble where the mother sat, upside down, head facing down toward the open bottom of the bubble: a small grey-brown spider with long legs, about one fourteenth of the frame width including the legs. Only one spider. No text, no watermark.

Edit this image. Keep the water surface, the plant stems, the pond bottom, the air bubble, the torn egg sac, the background, lighting and camera angle exactly the same. The young spider has grown into a large adult diving bell spider in the same place inside the air bubble: a dark brown body with long dark legs, about one sixth of the frame width including the legs, upside down, head facing down toward the open bottom of the bubble. Only one spider. No text, no watermark.

The spider keeps the same size, about one sixth of the frame width. Only one spider. No text, no watermark.
